race_context: La Porte Community School Corp. (LPCSC) serves the La Porte area of LaPorte County. The superintendent is Dr. Sandra Wood {hd_sea1}{hd_dest}. No current enrollment figure was found in the sources reviewed.

The board has seven members, all elected at large, with staggered terms. Four seats are elected in one cycle and three in the next: county records show the LPCSC at-large race as 'Vote for 4' in 2018 and 2022 and 'Vote for 3' in 2024 {lpc_2018res}{lpc_2022cand}{lpc_2024res}. The 2026 members are Ryan Seaburg (president), Tucker King (vice president), Monica Beaty (secretary), Jim Arnold, Jennifer Farlie, Nate Loucks and Amy Jackson {lpcsc_board}{hd_officers}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list says vote for 1, but four at-large seats are up. The Herald-Dispatch reported that the seat Loucks fills 'along with three other LPCSC school board seats' will be on the November ballot {hd_loucks}{in_list}. These are the four seats elected in 2022, when seven candidates ran and Farlie, Justin Holmquest, Jackson and Seaburg were on the ballot {lpc_2022cand}. Arnold, King and Beaty won the other three seats in 2024 and are not up this year {lpc_2024res}.

Who is running: incumbents Amy Jackson, Jennifer Farlie, Ryan Seaburg and Nate Loucks, plus newcomer Wendy (Swanson) Noren. That makes five candidates for four seats, all listed as Nonpartisan {in_list}{lpcsc_board}.

Board vacancy: Holmquest left the board after being named director of finance at New Prairie United School Corp. and resigned on Jan. 29, 2026 {hd_holmquest}{hd_loucks}. The board then picked Nate Loucks to fill the seat {hd_loucks}.

Budget and SEA 1: in September 2025 the Herald-Dispatch reported that LPCSC would lose an estimated $1.9 million because of the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) {hd_sea1}. In October 2026 the district set goals of becoming a 'destination district' and the highest-paying school district in Northwest Indiana by 2032 {hd_dest}.
Enrollment: on June 8, 2026, the board unanimously approved a resolution letting out-of-state students enroll {hd_outofstate}.
Policies: on March 9, 2026, the board unanimously approved buying Yondr cell phone pouches for the high, middle and intermediate schools for 2026-27 {hd_phones}.

Facilities and partnerships: on July 20, 2026, the board unanimously approved an updated easement agreement with Microsoft tied to its data center campus, and a lease agreement with Ivy Tech Community College; Jackson was absent {hd_msft}{hd_ivy}. A feasibility study on historic Kiwanis Field, done with Preserve Historic La Porte, was completed in September 2026 {hd_kiwanis}.
The Indiana School Boards Association gave the board an Exemplary Governance Award for 2024 {hd_isba}.

Forums: no 2026 LPCSC school board forum or questionnaire was found. The League of Women Voters of La Porte County announced two general-election candidate forums, but the coverage reviewed does not say whether school board candidates were included {hd_lwv}. A local group held an LPCSC candidate forum in 2024 {htn_2024}.

Coverage of these candidates is sparse. The local daily, the Herald-Dispatch, is paywalled past the opening of each article. No candidate statements on issues were found for any of the five candidates.
